cards.explanation: The answer is night, friends. The songwriter pairs the two: His loving devotion in the morning and His faithfulness at night (Psalm 92:2). So the singing covers sunrise and sundown. I bake early and I bake late, and apparently praise fits on that same schedule.

The answer is His deeds, friends. The songwriter says, “For You, O LORD, have made me glad by Your deeds; I sing for joy at the works of Your hands.” (Psalm 92:4) So the gladness comes from what the LORD has done. The song is a thank-you note with a tune.

The answer is True, friends. The songwriter says, “How great are Your works, O LORD, how deep are Your thoughts!” (Psalm 92:5) So the works are great and the thoughts are deep. Two compliments in one breath.

The answer is destroyed, friends. The songwriter says that though the wicked sprout like grass and all evildoers flourish, “…they will be forever destroyed.” (Psalm 92:7) Grass that shoots up fast looks impressive for a while. But the song says how it ends.

The answer is True, friends, and it's short and strong: “But You, O LORD, are exalted forever!” (Psalm 92:8) After all that talk about the wicked, the songwriter turns and points straight at the LORD. One line, no wasted words. I could learn something from that.

The answer is the downfall of his enemies, friends. The songwriter says, “My eyes see the downfall of my enemies…” (Psalm 92:11) That's what his eyes see. He doesn't say how or when it happened, only what he sees.

The answer is a palm tree, friends. The songwriter says, “The righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.” (Psalm 92:12) The wicked were grass. The righteous get a tree. That's quite the upgrade.
The answer is False, friends. The songwriter says, “In old age they will still bear fruit; healthy and green they will remain…” (Psalm 92:14) The word is still. Old age doesn't shut the bakery down.

The answer is to proclaim what the LORD is like, friends. The verse says they remain that way to proclaim, “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness.” (Psalm 92:15) So the song ends with the proclaiming, which is where it started. It opened with praise and it closes with praise.
